steps.say: VUR grading is performed carefully on voiding cystourethrography. Grades from Grade I to V are assigned by severity. Low grades are managed conservatively at first. Tortuosity with caliceal blunting is seen in Grade V. The worst demonstrated grade is recorded. Variation between voids is expected routinely in children.
steps.tx: **VUR grading** (reflux staging) by the International Reflux Study runs **Grade I to V** (one to five) on **VCUG** (voiding dye film), from urine flicking into the ureter to gross tortuosity with caliceal blunting at Grade V. Grade by the worst film, because reflux varies between voids.

steps.say: Primary reflux is caused by a short submucosal tunnel. A length to diameter ratio of 5:1 is considered normal. Flap-valve competence is lost when the tunnel shortens. Surgical lengthening is performed to restore the valve. Drugs are ineffective for purely anatomical reflux. Plumbing correction is surgically required for cure.
steps.tx: Primary reflux stems from a short **submucosal ureteral tunnel** (wall passage), because a healthy length to diameter ratio of **5:1** (five to one) shutters the **flap-valve competence** (one way valve) shut during filling. Lengthen the tunnel surgically to cure, because plumbing, not drugs, fixes the valve.

steps.say: The 99mTc-DMSA scan is ordered after febrile infections. Focal photon defects are shown clearly as scars. Differential function is measured accurately between the kidneys. Cortical scintigraphy is regarded as the gold standard. New defects are tracked carefully on repeat scanning. Surgical decisions are guided strongly by scar burden.
steps.tx: **99mTc-DMSA scan** (cortical scar photo, dimercaptosuccinic acid study) is the gold standard for **renal scarring** (kidney scars), showing focal photon defects and split function through **cortical scintigraphy** (rim imaging). Order it after febrile infections, because scars steer surgery. Repeat it yearly when reflux persists to track new defects.

vis.alt: Kidneys with obstruction, reflux, abscesses and management panels.
vis.caption: Reflux with scarring risk: DMSA maps defects that steer surgery. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Deflux is injected endoscopically for suitable mid grade reflux. The STING technique is performed under the orifice. The HIT procedure is added routinely with hydrodistension. Cure between 75 and 85 percent is reported. Day case treatment is completed safely without incisions. Tunnel coaptation is confirmed carefully on table.
steps.tx: **Deflux** (bulking gel) injected by the **STING technique** (under orifice injection) and **HIT procedure** (tunnel hydrodistension) cures **75%** to **85%** (three quarters to six sevenths) of Grades II to IV in a day case setting. Inject dextranomer hyaluronic acid to mound the orifice, because a longer coapted tunnel stops reflux.

steps.say: Cohen reimplantation is performed surgically across the trigone. A cross-trigonal submucosal tunnel is created surgically. Success between 95 and 98 percent is reported. High grade and failed Deflux cases are carefully selected. Open or robotic access is chosen according to anatomy. Diagonal length is guaranteed securely by design.
steps.tx: **Cohen reimplantation** (cross bladder tunnel, **cross-trigonal** (diagonal path)) tunnels the ureter across the trigone inside a new **submucosal tunnel** (wall sleeve) with open or robotic success of **95%** to **98%** (ninety five to ninety eight). It suits high grade or failed Deflux reflux, because the diagonal run guarantees length.

vis.alt: Intravenous urogram with grossly dilated collecting system.
vis.caption: High-grade reflux dilates the system: Cohen tunnelling restores the valve. Credit: Cambridge University Press.

steps.say: Leadbetter-Politano reimplantation is performed openly through the bladder. A fresh higher hiatus is created for the ureter. The neohiatus is sited above the old opening. Straight anatomy is preserved carefully for future endoscopy. The old hiatus is closed securely behind with sutures. Later ureteric access is kept reliably straightforward.
steps.tx: **Leadbetter-Politano** (new opening higher) reimplantation opens the bladder, pulls the ureter through a fresh higher hiatus, a **neohiatus** (new mouth), keeping straight anatomy for later endoscopy. Choose it when future ureteric access matters, because the natural line is preserved. Close the old hiatus securely to prevent diverticulum.

steps.say: Lich-Gregoir reimplantation is performed without opening the bladder. The detrusor is split down to intact mucosa. Extravesical reimplantation is completed neatly outside the lumen. Bleeding and spasms are minimised by the approach. Bilateral cases are finished efficiently together in one sitting. Overnight catheters are avoided safely whenever possible.
steps.tx: **Lich-Gregoir** (outside bladder repair) **extravesical reimplantation** (no bladder opening) splits detrusor to bare mucosa without entering the lumen, so bleeding and spasms stay minimal. It suits bilateral cases well, because both sides finish without catheters overnight. Stent the reimplant briefly when tunnels look tight.

steps.say: Bladder and bowel dysfunction is screened in every reflux child. Constipation is treated aggressively with regular laxatives. Timed voiding drills are taught patiently to families. Reflux is reassessed carefully after bowel regularity. Many low grades are resolved spontaneously without surgery. Persistent high grades are referred onwards for correction.
steps.tx: **Bladder and bowel dysfunction** (BBD (holding and constipation)) halves spontaneous resolution and doubles surgical failure, so treat constipation and timed voiding first. Reassess reflux after the bowel programme, because many low grades vanish with regularity. Add anticholinergics only when overactivity persists despite regularity.
